From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Variant-bundle discount and integration weighting

Hi Samantha / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching two high-level bundle options that trade off runtime footprint vs. premium support windows. Key asks from your side were: predictable TCO for year 1, a clear pilot credit to de-risk integration, and a migration/egress cap for the pilot period.

Two quick options (summary):
- Variant A (integration-first): 6-month pilot credit covering estimated integration throughput, 10% standard consumption discount thereafter, 1-week accelerated obs onboarding.
- Variant B (runtime-first): No pilot credit, deeper headline discount (15%) tied to a 12-month commit and a phased k-v cache migration plan.

We see integration effort as a multiplier on your overall cost of switching. To make comparisons easier I included an integration weighting column in the sheet so you can adjust the assumed engineering hours and see TCV impact.

Attachments: discount_calculator_v3.xlsx (interactive), proposal-v2.pdf (bundle descriptions).

Would you be open to a short call Wednesday to walk the spreadsheet and confirm the live throughput assumptions? If you can tell me an expected first-quarter consumption profile I can pin the numbers during the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa,

Thanks for the materials. A couple clarifications before we jump on a call:
1) Pilot credit — can you define the credit as a dollar cap rather than hours? Our finance team prefers a hard TCV cap.
2) The 15% for Variant B is attractive but our procurement policy requires at least one mid-year performance trigger tied to latency/accuracy SLAs before the second tranche releases.
3) Can you provide an estimated 0-12 month TCV under Variant A assuming our projected ramp (see below)?

Projected consumption: Month1 5M tokens, Month2 12M, Month3 25M, then steady 40M/month.

Finally, any flexibility on early onboarding credits if we commit to an enterprise plan by EOY?

Regards,
Procurement Team

Marissa, Jonas — quick playbook:

1) Offer a dollar-capped pilot credit equal to 60% of our estimated pilot consumption cost (based on their ramp) rather than an open-ended engineering credit. This gives them a clear cap and limits our exposure.

2) For Variant B, accept a two-stage performance release: 50% of the deeper discount up-front, remaining 50% contingent on meeting latency <200ms p95 and availability >99.5% for a 30-day window at month 6. Make metrics verifiable via our console logs (we can provide a read-only trace).

3) If they sign an enterprise-level 12-month commit by EOY, offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to $25k applied against month 1 invoices, plus a waived professional services coordination fee.

4) Keep the headline discount to a max of 15% (Variant B) and build in a recapture clause if consumption drops below 60% of forecast for any trailing 2-month period.

Jonas, support the numbers in the attached calculator (I tweaked the margin sensitivity). Marissa, propose these terms in writing and offer a 30-min walkthrough with their finance/eng team.

- Jordan
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

Samantha / Team — thanks for the clear ramp. Based on that, here's what we can commit to: 

- Pilot credit: $48,000 cap for the first 3 months (applies to Variant A pilot usage).
- Variant A post-pilot consumption discount: 10% standard; Variant B headline discount: 15% tied to a six-month performance trigger as described below.
- Performance release (Variant B): 50% of the deeper discount applied immediately; remaining 50% released after 30 consecutive days meeting latency <200ms p95 and availability >99.5%. Metrics will be visible via a read-only console link we provide.
- EOY enterprise-sign incentive: $25,000 onboarding credit and waived PS coordination fee if deal is fully executed by 2026-12-31.
- Recapture clause: if actual consumption falls <60% of forecast for rolling 2 months, pricing reverts to standard published rates until correction.

Attached: discount_calculator_v3.xlsx (tab updated with your ramp), proposal-v2.pdf (term language).

If this looks acceptable I'd like to schedule a 30-minute review with your finance and engineering stakeholders. I can also send a DocuSign for the pilot addendum and the enterprise term sheet.
